items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 22:1
items.html: The stature of the Nukva: behold, her place of emergence is in the head of ZA, upon the aspect of the Malchut of Ima, which is not included in the Mochin of ZA for the sake of his own Mochin. And upon this Malchut of Ima, in its inclusion with the crown of Gevura that is in the head of ZA, the Mochin of the Nukva emerge. And behold, this Malchut of Ima, upon which the Nukva holds, is not fit for Mochin, for it is the aspect of the second restriction; and the Mochin that emerge upon her are only through her inclusion in the crown of Gevura of ZA. Therefore she is discerned as needing ZA, namely the illumination of his crown of Gevura, for without this illumination she has no Mochin of the GAR. Hence she is smaller than him, for her Mochin are an offshoot of his Mochin, and come by means of their illumination, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 22:2
items.html: (To the question) However, the Mochin that she receives when she is in the back of ZA, which complete her stature equally with ZA from his back — behold, their place of emergence is in the Aba and Ima of AB, who are in the place of the GAR of AA, namely in that same place where ZA also receives his Mochin, and they are not at all from the aspect of the head of ZA. Therefore she does not need him — that is, she does not need to receive the illumination of his crown of Gevura, for she receives from the upper Ima herself, like ZA.
